Subject: SOC 2 Type II report + hosting and cross-border questions

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the call earlier. As part of our procurement and our internal risk review we need a couple of clarifications before we can move the contract to Legal:

- Do you have an available SOC 2 Type II report (most recent 12-month period) and can you share a redacted copy for our review?
- What is the audit period covered by the report? We need to understand whether it overlaps our expected go-live (Q3 2026).
- For EU-hosted workloads: can you confirm the physical hosting region(s) and whether customer content remains within the EU for processing and storage?
- Do you offer a formal bridge/attestation that covers cross-border data transfers for customers requiring EU-only residency during an audit gap? If so, what is the scope and typical language?
- Finally, we have a short SIG/CAIQ we will share; please confirm if you can populate a sample CAIQ snapshot and a control mapping for our use.

We are trying to complete our vendor security review by 2026-06-25. Appreciate a short reply with next steps and any artifacts you can share.

Best,
Sara Larsson
Head of Cloud Risk | NordicBank

Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II report + hosting and cross-border questions

Hi Sara — apologies for the delay, pulling the artifacts together now. Answers below and attached artifacts are referenced at the end.

1) SOC 2 Type II report - We can provide a redacted copy of our SOC 2 Type II report covering 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31. Attached: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025_redacted.pdf.

2) Audit period and coverage - The report covers the controls listed in the attestation across the full 12-month period above. Note: our next audit is scheduled for Q4 2026; if you need coverage beyond 2025-12-31 we can provide an interim bridge statement that attests to controls in-place as of the request date — see notes below on scope.

3) Hosting regions and residency - For EU customers we operate customer workloads in eu-west-1 (managed cluster fleet in Ireland) and eu-central-1 (Germany) depending on capacity and customer preference. Customer data stored and processed for EU-located deployments remains within the EU region. Control plane endpoints (metadata/orchestration) are operated from a separate control plane that may be hosted in the EU for private deployments and in a regional control plane for Dedicated customers; we can provide deployment-specific documentation.

4) Cross-border transfers and bridge attestations - We provide a standard bridge attestation letter when there is a gap between audit reports (type: interim attestation). Scope: confirms that the controls relevant to data residency and access controls remain implemented and monitored; does not include the full auditor re-performance. Typical language is included in the attached DPA_signed_redirect_link.txt (this file contains a pointer to our standard bridge wording and example language). For customers requiring stricter contractual residency we offer Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments and contractual addenda.

5) Artifacts requested (attached / links)
- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025_redacted.pdf (attached)
- CAIQ_snapshot_2026-05.json (attached) — this is a populated CAIQ subset for common questions
- control_mapping_nordicbank.xlsx (attached) — a custom mapping template we will fill based on your SIG
- DPA_signed_redirect_link.txt (attached) — link to our DPA and bridge wording examples

Notes on KMS / keys: for hosted EU deployments customers can opt to use our EU-resident KMS integration (keys in the EU region) or bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via customer-managed keys. Karthik, can you confirm the default for Dedicated vs Hosted?

Please let us know if you want us to redline or adapt the bridge language for your procurement team. If you share the SIG spreadsheet we will start populating the controls today.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Larsson <sara.larsson@nordicbank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 10:12:00 +0200
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II report + hosting and cross-border questions

Hi Sara — quick follow-up to clarify the hosting/KMS points so your architects can sign-off: 

- Control plane routing: For our Hosted (multi-tenant) offering we minimize cross-region traffic; however, some control plane telemetry may transit our global control plane depending on failover and telemetry aggregation. For Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) we can constrain control plane endpoints to the EU and provide documentation showing no egress to non-EU regions.
- KMS / keys: Default hosted customers use Redwood-managed KMS keys in the EU region for EU-hosted deployments. You can choose customer-managed keys (BYOK) via our EU KMS integrations if you require exclusive key control; this will keep encryption keys resident in the EU.
- Audit logs and retention: Logs for EU-hosted deployments are retained in-region and we can provide an export for audit purposes. The bridge attestation we provide can reference log retention policy and access controls, but final acceptance is a procurement/legal review item.

If you'd like, we can stand up a short technical session with our infra lead to walk through the network/dataflow diagrams and show tracelog examples.

Thanks,
Karthik
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
